notes: ILLUSTRATIVE. Concepts are listed in order of first_entry. A concept's explanation is shown only on the sentence that introduces it; its examples may use only forms with order <= first_entry (enforced by the sentence checker).

concepts.title: sein in the present: ich bin
concepts.explanation: 'bin' is the 'ich' form of 'sein' (to be). German verbs change their ending with the subject: ich bin, du bist, er ist.

examples.notes: Only 'ich' and 'bin' are known at order 2, so one example is the maximum.

concepts.title: Negation with nicht
concepts.explanation: 'nicht' negates a verb or phrase. It usually comes after the verb and its objects, and before adverbs of place: 'Er war nicht da.'
concepts.notes: Two examples: the vocabulary up to order 11 does not support a natural third.

concepts.title: sein in the past: war
concepts.explanation: 'war' is the simple past of 'sein' (to be). In everyday speech most verbs use the perfect tense for the past, but 'sein' normally uses 'war'.

concepts.title: ich war = er war
concepts.explanation: In the simple past, the 'ich' and 'er/sie/es' forms are identical: ich war, er war. Only the pronoun tells them apart.

examples.text: Ich war da, und sie war da.
examples.en: I was there, and she was there.
